environment.accelerator: CPU (XGBoost and scikit-learn do not use the Apple GPU/MPS here)

evaluation_note: Cluster agreement across the 5 implicates: mean ARI 0.88 (stable).
deployment_label: US household peer groups (Federal Reserve SCF 2022); not Indian benchmarks

datasets.name: Survey of Consumer Finances 2022, summary extract
datasets.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
datasets.observations: real survey responses; missing answers are multiply imputed by the Federal Reserve (5 implicates)
datasets.synthetic_observations: none (imputation of item non-response by the publisher is disclosed, not synthetic people)
datasets.licence: US Federal Reserve public data (no restriction stated on the page; cite the Federal Reserve)
datasets.preprocessing: 8 ratio features (see module docstring), clipped and signed-log compressed, standardised with survey weights.
datasets.missing_values: none after the publisher's imputation; families with income <= 0 excluded (counted)
datasets.known_biases: US households, 2022 dollars; wealthy households oversampled by design (weights correct for this).

methodology: Weighted K-Means on stacked implicates (weight WGT/5); k by silhouette; stability by ARI across implicates.
limitations: US households, not Indian; household-level, while a Finora profile may be one person; spending is not in the 2022 summary extract, so groups are about savings, debt and assets rather than spending habits.
reproducible: python -m app.ml.train peers (seed 7) with the raw file above
